content: Oligomenorrhea refers to the condition characterized by infrequent or light menstrual periods in women who are of reproductive age. This condition can sometimes be caused by prolactinomas, which are benign tumors of the anterior pituitary gland that result in excessive production of prolactin. Additionally, oligomenorrhea may also occur as a consequence of thyrotoxicosis, a condition of excessive thyroid hormone levels, or Graves' disease, an autoimmune disorder that leads to hyperthyroidism.
